text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

All dailies lead with the ruling by an Appeals Court in favour of Ekran Bhd, developer of the 13.6 billion ringgit ($5.5 billion) Bakun hydroelectric dam in the eastern Malaysian state of Sarawak on Borneo island.
-- Malaysia was ranked top in terms of returns on investment by a Malaysian banker's magazine.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said he wants Malaysians to preserve their unique qualities of racial harmony.
-- Mutiara Telecommunications Sdn Bhd is threatening to sue a local journalist and the Business Times newspaper for alleging that the company did not have a full licence to operate its services.

-- Commerce Asset Holdings Bhd and the New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd have signed an equity restructuring deal to strengthen American Malaysian Life Assurance Sdn Bhd's position in the insurance industry.
-- Petronas, the Malaysian national oil company, said it sees no disagreement or problems with its participation in Vietnam's Dung Quat refinery project.
